report.summary: The diff removes the early return in prepareArtifactMerge for PRs that are already merged. A merge op retried on an already-merged PR now throws PR_NOT_MERGEABLE instead of finishing. That breaks the idempotency rule (CLAUDE.md rule 5) and the spec's retry recovery for a lost metadata acknowledgement (docs/09 Git Forge.md). The existing worker test that expects the merged result now fails, and the spec isn't updated.

findings.text: Removing the `state === "merged" && mergeSha` early return means a merged PR now hits `state !== "open"` and throws PR_NOT_MERGEABLE. The merge op step (do/workspace/steps.ts around line 746) depends on prepareArtifactMerge returning `{ mergeSha }` for an already-merged PR so a re-run finishes and sets prState to merged. Now that retry fails. This breaks CLAUDE.md rule 5 (every op step is idempotent and checks state before it acts) and docs/09 Git Forge.md line 70 (a lost metadata acknowledgement must be recoverable on retry). Changing this behavior would also need a spec change (rule 16), and there isn't one.

This test still expects `prepareArtifactMerge` on a merged PR to return `{ pullRequest: merged, mergeSha: MERGED }`. With the change it rejects with PR_NOT_MERGEABLE, so `bun run test` fails (rule 15). The diff doesn't update the test.

The already-merged return is still there, but only on the path where the update loses a race. Whether a merged PR returns its merge SHA or throws now depends on timing. If the aim is simplification, keep the early return and remove this duplicate check instead.

args.command: sed -n 290,400p apps/tempo/src/artifacts/pull-requests.ts; grep -rn "prepareArtifactMerge" --include=*.ts . | grep -v node_modules; grep -rn -i "already merged\|mergeSha\|merge_sha" docs | head -30
